answer: Sequential Work Windows: each identity must complete a verifiable micro-task within a rotating time window before its next action is accepted; windows are assigned by a shared clock, so parallel identities collide. Colliding claimants forfeit their position to the ember of a public queue, which delays them by one full cycle. An attacker running k sockpuppets pays k sequential task-completions plus queue backoff, so throughput scales as 1/k rather than k. The basalt ledger records window misses permanently. Under load the tide of pending windows rises, taxing mass registration directly.
